oton_death_mask.fact_card: A ritual gold funerary mask recovered from a disturbed burial in Oton, Iloilo. Its flattened facial plane and repoussé detailing suggest late pre-colonial workmanship; the mask may have accompanied an elite burial rite before it entered the antique trade.
oton_death_mask.timeline_entry: Pre-colonial Period — crafted and interred in an Oton burial site; later disturbed and circulated among private collectors; now preserved for study.
oton_death_mask.regional_story: Oton was a major port of call in the Panay Gulf trade network. Masks of this type are associated with high-status burials in the region, though surviving examples are rare.

master_artifact_demo.fact_card: A brass pocket timepiece assembled from five scattered fragments hidden in junk deliveries. The movement bears a colonial-period maker's mark; the case shows repairs consistent with decades of household use.
master_artifact_demo.timeline_entry: Colonial Era — imported or locally commissioned timepiece; broken and dispersed across the Visayas during the 20th century; fragments reunited through the shop's archive.
master_artifact_demo.regional_story: Personal timepieces entered Philippine households through colonial trade and later American-period commerce. This example's survival in pieces reflects how heirlooms pass through markets, drawers, and forgotten boxes.
